question: Teenagers and K-pop fans claimed to have booked vast numbers of free tickets to a 2020 Trump rally in Tulsa. Did that keep supporters out?
options: Yes: fans held most of the seats
No: sign-ups did not reserve seats
Partly: fans took about half the seats
answer: No. Entry was first come, first served, and registering reserved no seat, so a fake sign-up could not block a real supporter. What the pranks inflated was the campaign's forecast: it boasted of over a million requests, yet the fire department counted about 6,200 people inside a 19,000-seat arena. The empty seats had other causes.
move: Before crediting a cause, check it could have produced the effect.
ask: Before I credit a cause, could it actually have produced that effect?
trap: Crediting the prank because it came just before the empty seats.

reference: Taylor Lorenz, Kellen Browning and Sheera Frenkel, TikTok Teens and K-Pop Stans Say They Sank Trump Rally, The New York Times, 21 June 2020
